```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
log_file <- system.file("extdata", "dietview_example_worms_log.csv", package = "DietView")
has_log  <- nzchar(log_file)
```

DietView can attach a taxonomic lineage to every prey by querying the
[World Register of Marine Species (WoRMS)](https://www.marinespecies.org/). This
vignette shows how to run the lookup, how to read the log of how each prey was
matched, and how to freeze the result so that later runs need no network. The
lookup chunks are shown but not run, because they need the `worrms` package and
an internet connection.

## Why a lineage, and why unidentified records stay

DietView shows the diet at seven ranks, kingdom to species, by default. Your
records rarely carry all seven: identification often stops at a coarse rank
(`Decapoda`, `Teleostei`). DietView never fills in the missing ranks. Below the
last rank reached, the record is shown as unidentified at that rank, so every
ring of the sunburst still holds all the records and adds up to 100%.

## Running the lookup

`dv_prepare(taxonomy = "worms")` calls `dv_taxonomy_worms()` once for each
distinct prey key, not once per record.

```{r prepare}
library(DietView)

dat <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "dietview_example.csv", package = "DietView"),
  na.strings = c("NA", "")
)
spec <- dv_spec(
  predator  = "predator_species_latin_name",
  stomach   = "stomach_id",
  prey_id   = "aphia_id",
  prey_name = "verified_name",
  weight    = "prey_weight"
)

prep <- dv_prepare(dat, spec, taxonomy = "worms")
prep
```

## How each prey is matched

Each distinct prey gets one row in the log, with a `match_type`:

| `match_type` | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | The AphiaID is accepted in WoRMS | Nothing, unless `name_check` is `"differs"` |
| `id_synonym` | The AphiaID is unaccepted; its accepted ID was used | Check that the accepted name is the taxon you meant |
| `id_unchecked` | WoRMS could not be reached to check the ID | Run again later |
| `exact` | No ID; the name matched exactly | Nothing |
| `fuzzy` | No ID; the name was matched by TAXAMATCH, which tolerates misspellings | Check every one: a near match can be a different taxon |
| `unresolved` | No match | Correct the name, or accept that the prey stays unidentified |

Two more columns flag problems. `name_check` is `"differs"` when the name in
your table is not the name WoRMS holds for that AphiaID, which usually means
that one of the two was mistyped. `lineage_ok` is `FALSE` when the prey was
matched but WoRMS returned no classification, for example because the
connection failed. Those prey count as unidentified at every rank until you run
the lookup again. Failed lookups are not stored in the cache, so the next run
asks WoRMS again.

Successful lookups are cached on disk (in `tools::R_user_dir("DietView", "cache")`),
so a rerun only queries what changed. The log also records when the taxonomy
was retrieved and which `worrms` version was used, in its `retrieved` and
`worrms_version` attributes.

## Reading the report

`dv_taxonomy_report()` returns the prey that need a look, largest number of
records first:

```{r report}
review <- dv_taxonomy_report(prep, which = "review")
review

# the whole log, to archive or to send to a co-author
dv_taxonomy_report(prep, which = "all", file = file.path(tempdir(), "taxonomy_log.csv"))
```

```{r frozen-intro, eval = TRUE, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
if (has_log) {
  cat("The package ships the full log of one such run on the example table,",
      "so you can see what a report looks like without a connection:\n")
} else {
  cat("A frozen copy of this log (`dietview_example_worms_log.csv`) is not",
      "included in this build of the package, so the chunk below is not run.\n")
}
```

```{r frozen, eval = has_log}
wlog <- read.csv(log_file, na.strings = c("NA", ""))
wlog[, intersect(c("prey_name", "prey_id", "match_type", "name_check",
                   "matched_name", "n_records", "lineage_ok"), names(wlog))]
```

On this table, "unidentified material" has neither an AphiaID nor a
taxonomic name, so it is `unresolved`, and its records are unidentified at
every rank. That is expected. Unresolved prey you did not expect are the ones
to chase.

## Correcting and freezing

Fix the names or IDs the report lists in your source table and run the lookup
again. When the log is clean, save the lineage and switch to the offline path
for every later run:

```{r fix}
lineage <- unique(prep$data[, c(spec$prey_name, prep$ranks)])
write.csv(lineage, "lineage_2026-10-20.csv", row.names = FALSE)

lineage <- read.csv("lineage_2026-10-20.csv", na.strings = c("NA", ""))
prep <- dv_prepare(dat, spec, taxonomy = "table", lineage = lineage)
```

The lineage table fixes the taxonomic snapshot your figures were made from.
Archive it with your data, and note the retrieval date and the `worrms`
version, because WoRMS changes.

## Exact matching only

To turn off TAXAMATCH matching and keep only known AphiaIDs and exact names:

```{r conservative}
prep <- dv_prepare(dat, spec, taxonomy = "worms", fuzzy = FALSE)
```
